name: Dryer Motor Circuit Resistance (Door to Motor Path)
purpose: Quick check of motor circuit wiring and motor from control neutral/door switch to motor relay — isolates harness vs motor vs control.
failureModes: Open (OL): broken harness, door switch, belt switch, or motor winding
1–6 Ω with drum still not running: motor circuit acceptable — suspect control board relay
testingTips: Measure with power disconnected per manufacturer test points (often door/neutral to motor relay)
If in range but motor won't run, verify belt switch toggles and door switch closes (0–2 Ω)

name: Dryer Exhaust (Outlet) Thermistor Resistance
purpose: Verify exhaust thermistor at CCU connector — used for heat control and airflow detection (F3E1 open, F3E2 short on many models).
failureModes: >50 kΩ (open): F3E1 — exhaust thermistor open, temp reads below ~18°F
<0.5 kΩ (short): F3E2 — shorted thermistor, temp reads above ~250°F
5–15 kΩ at room on connector: often acceptable before condemning sensor
testingTips: Unplug dryer and remove thermistor connector from control before measuring
At ~70°F expect roughly 11–14 kΩ; use manufacturer table when available
Check pins to cabinet ground — continuity indicates shorted harness
notes: Values at P14 outlet thermistor connector — temperature-dependent; note ambient when comparing

name: Dryer Inlet Thermistor Resistance (Electric)
purpose: Verify inlet thermistor on electric dryers (often part of high-limit assembly) — assists airflow and load detection.
failureModes: Both inlet and exhaust open: check thermistor harness connector at control
testingTips: At ~68°F (20°C) expect roughly 61–64 kΩ on many Whirlpool-style electric dryers
Measure at control connector with power off and connector removed

name: Dryer Inlet Thermistor Resistance (Gas)
purpose: Verify inlet thermistor at drum inlet duct on gas dryers — used with exhaust thermistor for airflow faults.
failureModes: F3E5: both inlet and exhaust open — harness unplugged at control
testingTips: At ~68°F expect roughly 58–68 kΩ on many Whirlpool-style gas dryers
Gas inlet thermistor curve differs from electric — do not use electric table

name: Dryer Exhaust Air Temperature (Vent Outlet)
purpose: Verify exhaust temperature during timed dry (empty drum, vent disconnected) — validates thermistor and heat control.
failureModes: Fails to reach setpoint in ~7 min: vent blockage, low voltage, or weak heat circuit
Runs hot above spec: restricted vent, failed high-limit path, or stuck heat relay
testingTips: Timed dry, empty drum, external vent disconnected, EcoBoost off
High ~155°F heat-off, Medium ~140°F, Low ~125°F, Extra Low ~105°F (±5°F typical)
Heat turns back on ~10–15°F below heat-off point
notes: Setting-specific targets — record which cycle/temp level was used

name: Dryer Thermal Cut-Off Continuity
purpose: Verify thermal cut-off continuity — opens on overheat; pair-replace with high-limit when failed.
failureModes: Open (OL): no heat — replace thermal cut-off AND high-limit thermostat together
Often caused by vent restriction — clear airflow before replacing parts only
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing at cut-off terminals
On gas and electric dryers, cut-off is in the heater gas/element path ahead of high-limit
